description:
We can hear the waves crash, the bird sing, the leaves of a tree rustle but, can we hear the changes that happen to our planet? 

Our team is aiming to create a tool that translates planetary events visualizations into audio using computer vision and interactive tools that connect users from across the globe to create and listen to the earth sing.
summary:
Asteria’s Song is an interactive web experience that turns NASA Earth observation imagery into sound, so that blind and visually impaired people can explore what satellites see.

Satellite images are mostly visual, which leaves many people out. Earth Jukebox translates eight Earth phenomena into sound: ocean currents, forest fires, air quality, aerosols, night lights, aurora, hurricanes and lightning. Visitors hover over (or tab to) a symbol on an illustrated world map and instantly hear a sound designed to represent it. Each one also has a short spoken audio description, available with one press of a speaker button, which explains the phenomenon and links to the related NASA data. The site works with a keyboard and screen readers, and needs no installation.

Built with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Tone.js, and hosted on GitHub Pages.
details:
Name: Asteria’s Song: Earth Jukebox
Challenge: NASA Space Apps challenge 2026
Live demo: https://nadynstary.github.io/Astria-s-Song/
Code: https://github.com/nadynstary

The problem

NASA’s Earth observation data is mostly shared as images, maps and animations. Blind and visually impaired people can’t access most of it, so they are left out of a huge part of what satellites reveal about our planet.

Our solution

Asteria’s Song uses sonification, which means translating visual information into sound. Visitors explore an illustrated world map with eight Earth phenomena: ocean currents, forest fires, air quality, aerosols, night lights, aurora, hurricanes and lightning. Each one has its own sound that plays instantly when the visitor hovers over its icon or tabs to it with the keyboard.

How it works

  1. The visitor opens the site and clicks once. Browsers require this before any sound can play.
  2. Hovering over or focusing an icon plays that phenomenon’s sound and opens an info box.
  3. The info box has a short written description, a link to the related NASA data, and a speaker button that plays a spoken audio description of the phenomenon.
  4. Moving to another icon switches the sound. The description can be stopped with the button or the Escape key.

Accessibility features

  • Sound-first design: each phenomenon can be recognized by its sound alone.
  • Spoken audio descriptions for every event, so nothing depends on reading text.
  • Full keyboard navigation (Tab to an icon, Tab to the speaker, Enter to play).
  • Screen-reader labels on all interactive elements. Decorative visuals are hidden from assistive technology.
  • Reduced-motion support for the animated backgrounds.
  • No installation, accounts or downloads. It runs in any modern browser.

Sound design

Each sound is designed to suggest its phenomenon, for example flowing arpeggios for ocean currents, warm pulses with crackles for fires, and a slow, dreamy pad for the aurora. [Say how the hurricane and lightning sounds were made, and whether any sounds use real data or recordings.]

NASA data and resources

https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/5669/

https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/3912/#media_group_349716

https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/13786/

https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/5011/

Technology

HTML5, CSS3, vanilla JavaScript and Tone.js for real-time sound. It is hosted for free on GitHub Pages, so it’s easy for anyone to open and reuse.

Challenges and what we learned

Browsers block audio until the visitor interacts with the page, so we designed the first click around that. We also learned how strict file naming is on web hosting, and how much care accessible design needs.

Future work

  • Drive the sounds with real NASA datasets (for example, fire intensity controlling crackle density, or aerosol thickness controlling brightness).
  • Test with blind and visually impaired users and improve the design from their feedback.
  • Add more phenomena and more languages, including Arabic.
  • Add an option to adjust volume and playback speed.
